due_when.clears_when: an operator or a future session decides whether registered_soak_logs()/pipeline_ids() should fold to current state instead of scanning raw, and (if so) makes the change

what: scripts/ci/check_soak_registered.py's registered_soak_logs() and scripts/ops/check_allow_degraded.py's pipeline_ids() both scan the pipeline store's UNFOLDED raw record stream (pipeline.py's new LoadResult.raw), so an id ever seen in an OPEN state (queued/due/routed) counts as 'registered'/'citable' FOREVER, even after a later record closes it (done/killed). MEASURED 2026-09-24 while re-pointing both guards to the directory store (lane E64): bybit_coverage_soak is 'registered' only via a record now superseded by a killed state (line 46 queued, line 1393 killed in the pre-migration flat file). This is the PRE-EXISTING behaviour (verified identical against the original flat-file parsers: 11 registered soaks / 824 open ids, both unchanged by the re-point) -- E64 preserved it byte-for-byte rather than deciding it, since changing it would silently newly-fail bybit_coverage_soak and ict_scalp_exit_head_soak in an unrelated storage-migration PR. Is 'once registered, always citable' the intended rule, or should both guards fold to CURRENT state (pipeline.read_log().items) so a closed row stops counting? A session with the room to make that call should decide and, if folding is correct, re-file any soak/annotation that would newly fail.
